summary: This bash script automatically generates markdown documentation from shell script source code. It scans helper scripts in a directory, extracts specially-marked comment blocks (regions), converts them to markdown format, creates a table of contents, and generates individual documentation files with an auto-generated banner indicating they shouldn't be manually edited.

explanations.5: This command finds the absolute path of the directory containing this script itself (not the directory where the script is being run from). It changes into that directory, suppresses error output, and captures the result with pwd.
explanations.38: The 'local -n' syntax creates a nameref—a reference to another variable. So 'arr' becomes an alias pointing to whatever array name was passed as argument $1, letting us modify the original array.
explanations.41: IFS (Internal Field Separator) is temporarily set to newline so the array elements are split by newlines instead of spaces. The sort command processes the array as multi-line input, then the results are stored in a new array.
explanations.85: The '-r' flag makes the variable read-only, preventing accidental modification. This is a safety measure for variables that shouldn't change after being set.
explanations.91: This sed command finds lines between the start and end tags (inclusive) and prints only those lines—it's extracting a block from the file.
explanations.131: The '${2:-}' syntax means 'use argument 2 if provided, otherwise use an empty string.' The hyphen-colon provides a default value when the variable is unset.
explanations.178: This sets startTag to argument 3 if provided, otherwise defaults to 'public function'. The '^' prefix means 'at the beginning of a line' in regex patterns used later with sed.
explanations.200: mktemp creates a temporary file with a unique name and returns its path. This is safer than hardcoding a filename because it avoids conflicts.
explanations.254: The sed command inserts text (the 'i' flag) at line 1 (before anything else) into the file. The backslash escapes allow literal newlines in the insertion.
explanations.316: This uses the find command to locate all .sh files in the helpers subdirectory and stores the results as a newline-separated string (not yet an array).
explanations.330: This bash parameter expansion replaces '%.sh' at the end of the filename with '.md'. The '%' means 'match at the end of the string.'
explanations.332: Similarly, this replaces the first occurrence of '/helpers/' directory name with '/documentation/' to change where the output file goes.
explanations.406: This removes Windows-style carriage returns (\r) from the headings. The double slash means 'replace all occurrences,' making it compatible across Unix and Windows line endings.
explanations.422: The '[[ ... =~ ... ]]' syntax tests if the heading string matches the regex pattern. If it matches, the BASH_REMATCH array gets populated with captured groups.
explanations.425: BASH_REMATCH[1] gets the first captured group (text inside parentheses) from the regex—in this case, the slug text without the curly braces.
explanations.434: This string replacement changes markdown heading syntax from '##' (level 2) to '#' (level 1), effectively promoting the heading level for the table of contents.
explanations.439: Replaces each '#' with '* ' to convert markdown headings into bullet points. The space after the asterisk is important for markdown formatting.
explanations.440: Replaces any remaining '#' characters with two spaces for indentation, creating nested list structure based on heading depth.
explanations.468: The '<(...)' syntax is process substitution—it treats the output of printf as a file that the while loop reads from, line by line.
explanations.505: Uses the '-r' read-only flag again for safety, and '${1:-[:space:]}' provides a default character class (any whitespace) if no argument is given.
explanations.506: The sed pattern finds characters at the start of the line and removes them. The escaping with '\%' prevents the '%' itself from being interpreted as a special character.
